$comment: Per-route performance budgets. The single authority for the build gate and,
when it lands, the Lighthouse CI assertion config -- section 22 requires the
budget to live in configuration, and two configuration files would be the
two-sources defect wearing another costume.
Section 22: 'every route in the CI budget file carries a numeric threshold',
with 180KB critical-path JS and LCP under 2.5s on throttled 4G as the default
for any route that has not ratified its own. So `status` records PROVENANCE --
where a number came from -- and never replaces the number. A route whose
status is `inherited` still states its threshold explicitly, because a reader
checking compliance must not have to resolve a default in their head.
180KB is read as 180000 bytes, not 184320. The conservative reading.
status:
inherited   takes the default; the number is copied here deliberately
explicit    ratified its own ceiling; `reason` is mandatory
exempt      not gated; `reason` is mandatory
Raising a threshold is its own commit, carrying the measured number and the
reason. Never in the commit that made it red.
A stable proxy for transfer size, not a prediction of it: a real CDN may
use a different level or Brotli and will land lower. Validated against
the running production server at 0.25% difference.
Excludes the legacy `noModule` polyfill bundle, which no browser that
understands ES modules ever requests. Including it cost 39520 B and put
the employee route over the default on the first measurement -- an
exemption earned by bytes nobody downloads.

$comment: Section 22's 'throttled 4G' is the condition. Recorded here so the
threshold is not mistaken for one measured on an unthrottled desktop.
Lighthouse cannot measure INP -- it is a navigation test with no real
interaction -- so TBT stands in there and interaction latency is
measured in Playwright instead.
Framework routes, carrying almost no application code. They are here as
the cheapest early warning that exists: when the Next or React baseline
grows, these move first and for a reason that is not our doing.
